### 2. preview-token-apply-route-binding

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Diagnosis | Every named apply route is provenance-blind. In `src/RoslynMcp.Host.Stdio/Tools/RefactoringTools.cs` the five `*_apply` shims (`rename_apply` L44-55, `organize_usings_apply` L75-86, `format_document_apply` L106-117, `code_fix_apply` L141-152, `format_range_apply` L178-189) each call `ToolDispatch.ApplyByTokenAsync(gate, previewStore, previewToken, c => refactoringService.ApplyRefactoringAsync(previewToken, "<route>", c), ct)`. The route-name string is a response/telemetry label only — it is never compared against the token's producer, so any `IPreviewStore` token (e.g. one minted by `ParameterObjectService.PreviewAsync`, `src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Services/ParameterObjectService.cs:135`) redeems on any of those routes and mutates the workspace. `ToolDispatch.ApplyByTokenAsync` (`src/RoslynMcp.Host.Stdio/Tools/ToolDispatch.cs:114-133`) is the single shared redemption seam: it peeks the workspace id, opens the write gate, revalidates the write set (`RevalidateChangedPathsAsync`, L129), then invokes the service call — but performs no producer check. The generic verified route `apply_with_verify` (`src/RoslynMcp.Host.Stdio/Tools/ApplyWithVerifyTool.cs:26-41`) is worse: it bypasses `ApplyByTokenAsync` entirely, peeks `previewStore.PeekWorkspaceId` itself (L34) and hands the raw token to `IApplyUndoWorkflowService.ApplyWithVerifyAsync`, with no statement anywhere of which producers it supports. Its `[Description]` (L25) says only "a previously previewed refactoring". Sibling `preview-token-store-provenance-contract` adds the producer discriminator to `IPreviewStore`/`PreviewStore`; this slice is the consumer half — acceptance bullets 2-4 plus the cross-route regression. |
| Approach | 1. `src/RoslynMcp.Host.Stdio/Tools/ToolDispatch.cs` — add an OPTIONAL parameter `string? expectedProducer = null` (or `IReadOnlyCollection<string>? acceptedProducers = null` if the sibling's discriminator is an enum-shaped string set) to `ApplyByTokenAsync`, and a private `RequireCompatibleProducer(previewStore, previewToken, accepted, routeName)` guard invoked INSIDE `gate.RunWriteAsync` immediately BEFORE `RevalidateChangedPathsAsync` at L129 — i.e. before any mutation, mirroring the existing pre-mutation revalidation pattern. Guard semantics mirror the documented `PeekChangedPaths` null-means-"unknown, skip — never verified" convention (`src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Contracts/IPreviewStore.cs:106-119`): a null/absent discriminator skips enforcement so out-of-tree stores and the three local `FakePreviewStore` doubles keep compiling; a PRESENT-and-incompatible discriminator throws before mutation. Optional-with-default is load-bearing — `ApplyByTokenAsync` has 15 production callers (see Risks), and a required parameter would force edits in all of them. 2. `src/RoslynMcp.Host.Stdio/Tools/RefactoringTools.cs` — pass the compatible producer set at each of the five named apply shims (L50, L81, L112, L147, L184); one added argument per call, no body restructuring. 3. `src/RoslynMcp.Host.Stdio/Tools/ApplyWithVerifyTool.cs` — after the existing `PeekWorkspaceId` resolution (L34) and inside `gate.RunWriteAsync` before `workflowService.ApplyWithVerifyAsync` (L41), enforce the generic route's supported set (every `IPreviewStore`-produced solution-snapshot token; composite/project-mutation-store tokens are structurally out of reach here), and extend its `[Description]` (L25) to state that supported set explicitly per acceptance bullet 2. 4. Error shape: reuse the actionable-envelope precedent of `PreviewTokenStaleException` (`src/RoslynMcp.Core/Services/PreviewTokenStaleException.cs`) — the message MUST name the token's actual producer AND the expected apply route ("token was produced by `parameter_object_preview`; redeem it via `apply_with_verify`, not `rename_apply`"). Prefer a distinct exception type only if the sibling's contract does not already supply one; otherwise `InvalidOperationException` routed through `ToolErrorHandler` is sufficient — do NOT re-open `IPreviewStore`/`PreviewStore`. |
| Scope | Production files: 3 — `src/RoslynMcp.Host.Stdio/Tools/ToolDispatch.cs`, `src/RoslynMcp.Host.Stdio/Tools/RefactoringTools.cs`, `src/RoslynMcp.Host.Stdio/Tools/ApplyWithVerifyTool.cs`. Within the Rule 3 cap of 4; no exemption claimed. `ToolDispatch.cs` is one file beyond the pre-split slice's declared two-file list and is deliberate: it is the single shared redemption seam, and enforcing in the tool bodies instead would duplicate the same guard six times (Directive #3 copy-paste smell). `IPreviewStore.cs` / `PreviewStore.cs` are NOT touched — the discriminator is consumed only, per the slice boundary. At the Rule 4 cap of 3. |
